subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: What closure bar should #87109 use: macOS launchd soak proof under #54155, or a separate durable cron failure-reporting design that does not depend on a healthy Gateway event loop?
rationale: The remaining gap is not one obvious code edit: source shows partial memory and cron recovery fixes, but deciding whether in-process restart recovery is sufficient requires maintainer intent and representative proof.

options.title: Keep As Mac Cron Subtracker
options.body: Require a macOS launchd soak with memory/dreaming/cron workload proof before closing or merging remaining fixes.

options.title: Split Failure Reporting
options.body: Move the out-of-process or restart-aware cron alert design to a narrower product issue while leaving RSS growth under #54155.

options.title: Close After Partial Fixes
options.body: Treat #86701, #86783, #100867, and v2026.6.11 mitigations as enough, accepting that the cron alert gap is unproven.

recommendation.title: Keep As Mac Cron Subtracker
recommendation.body: Require a macOS launchd soak with memory/dreaming/cron workload proof before closing or merging remaining fixes.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest owner signal for the canonical Gateway RSS soak/profiling closure bar that this issue overlaps.
